rows.oneLine: FrontStrike competitive gaming product with a verified Solana devnet program.
rows.whatItBuilds: PrimeSkill Studio developed FrontStrike, a competitive gaming product using a Solana devnet program and a devnet test token.
rows.finding: Mainnet deployment was not verified and the official X account was suspended when checked. The devnet program recorded 443 signatures with a 91.87% success rate; its latest observed activity was 20 September 2025.
rows.nextAction: Founder verification is required to confirm whether FrontStrike migrated, paused or was abandoned.

rows.oneLine: Climate-data infrastructure with live SST dashboards and a pre-mainnet Solana layer.
rows.whatItBuilds: END Corp operates public sea-surface-temperature data products and is developing decentralised satellite ground-station and token infrastructure.
rows.finding: The public climate dashboard is live and updated daily. All verified END Corp program and token addresses were on Solana devnet; no known mainnet address was found.
rows.nextAction: Validate the devnet findings with the founder and request a production deployment address when mainnet launches.

rows.oneLine: A consumer and DePIN concept with insufficient public product or chain evidence.
rows.whatItBuilds: The directory positions Home Harvest across consumer and DePIN, but the available public presence did not provide enough material to validate a live product or blockchain deployment.
rows.finding: The reviewed X page contained no usable product evidence. No verified mainnet deployment, public contract or measurable user activity was identified.
rows.nextAction: Ask the founder for the product URL, current build status, user metrics and any devnet or mainnet deployment.

rows.oneLine: A short-form playable-game feed that supported a large no-code game jam.
rows.whatItBuilds: Scrolly was a feed for instantly playable games, shared points, leaderboards and developer distribution. The founder confirmed that activity and Coinflow payments were off-chain.
rows.finding: No official token or public Scrolly program was verified. Public records support 300 submissions as a project-reported count, while 27 games and 25 developers were individually named in the public census. Production ended on 26 June 2026.
rows.nextAction: Retain as a historical ecosystem-support case study and keep platform-wide claims separate from named developer evidence.

rows.oneLine: Fanplay evolved into WTF Games after moving its crypto-payment rails to Solana.
rows.whatItBuilds: Fanplay launched live-event wagering using USDC, first on Arbitrum and later on Solana, before evolving into the WTF Games crypto-casino brand.
rows.finding: Mainnet use is supported by official migration and product evidence, but no operational wallet, treasury, vault, program ID or verified transaction has been publicly documented. Public evidence indicates a hybrid model where crypto payments may be on-chain while wagering logic remains internal.
rows.nextAction: Identify one legitimate deposit, withdrawal or bet transaction, verify the receiving entity and expand it into an operational-wallet cluster.
